hints: Notice the three momentum magnitudes: $mu$ before, and $Mu/3$ at angle $\alpha$ above plus $mu/2$ at angle $\beta$ below after.
Recall vector conservation: the vector sum of the two after-collision momenta must equal the single before-collision vector $mu$ to the right.
Check the triangle by head-to-tail addition and match each interior angle to the correct scattered particle - $\alpha$ with the $M$ track and $\beta$ with the $m$ track.
walkthrough: Write the momenta as vectors. Before: $p = mu$ to the right. After: $p_M = Mu/3$ at $\alpha$ above the horizontal and $p_m = mu/2$ at $\beta$ below the horizontal.
Apply conservation of vector momentum: $mu = p_M + p_m$. So $p_M$ and $p_m$ placed head-to-tail must start at the tail of $mu$ and finish at the tip of $mu$.

This requires the $mu/2$ arrow to leave the left end of the $mu$ arrow going down, and the $Mu/3$ arrow to arrive at the right end of the $mu$ arrow coming from below. Diagrams with opposite arrows give $-mu$.
Match the angles. At the right tip, the $Mu/3$ side makes angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal $mu$ side. At the left tail, the $mu/2$ side makes angle $\beta$ with the horizontal $mu$ side.
Only the triangle with $\beta$ on the left, $\alpha$ on the right, and the correct head-to-tail sense satisfies both the magnitude directions and the angle positions. This is option B.

A.explanation: Arrow directions close the triangle correctly, but the angles are swapped. Angle $\alpha$ belongs with $Mu/3$ and angle $\beta$ belongs with $mu/2$.

B.explanation: The two after-collision momenta $Mu/3$ and $mu/2$ placed head-to-tail give resultant $mu$, and $\alpha$ is at the $Mu/3$ end while $\beta$ is at the $mu/2$ end.

C.explanation: Both the angles are swapped and the $mu/2$ and $Mu/3$ arrows are reversed, so head-to-tail addition gives $-mu$ instead of $mu$.

D.explanation: The angles are in the correct places but the $mu/2$ and $Mu/3$ arrows are reversed, so the triangle represents $mu + Mu/3 + mu/2 = 0$ rather than conservation.
